questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the Erasmus coordinator at Statale university, and the ones in Copenhagen are generally very helpful and flexible

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Directions to how to register,and get the first signature to my proof of attendance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think that you are very left on your own in terms of  finding courses that exists, fits your degree and are in english

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used the website Spotahome which worked fine, and had sort of a security deposit, ensuring that neither me or my landlord got scammed the first month, but we lived 3 people in a 2-bedroom appartment, so in general it was very difficult to find housing that is affordable!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it can be very expensive, and that it isn't a must to live very central in Milano, other areas are just as nice and more affordable and local.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sort of difficult, but they had a window of 2 weeks in the beginning, where it was possible to change courses, which helped a lot

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to find them in the course catalogue, and see if it didn't overlap in your own schedule. But then you could register and change your registration at the unimia platform

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Hmm, not much

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end it worked out

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you find a course you think is interesting, try to see if other courses at the same master is available for you, that way they don't overlap in time, and your understanding of each course will get better

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Even though i only had master-classes i think the level was fine for most of my courses, as the were sort of introductionary and the italian students attending them had a lot of different bachelors. But for instance, my course about geopolitics of migration was the most difficult one, as I didn't really have much preliminary knowledge of this field of social science.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, and a bit more old-school, in the way that you don't have to read/prepare before lectures, as you do in Copenhagen, and there is not  a lot of interaction with students or discussions on most courses. But in general the teachers were very passionate, which helps

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Narrating and negotiating identities
Geopolitics of Migration
Journalism, media and politics
Globalization, social justice and human rights

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Narrating and negotiating identities! I thought this course had a very interesting perspective on migration, and was a lot more critical, and student-engaging than my other courses. This one offered autonomus analyzing instead of "just" learning the curriculum in the correct way.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Registration fee for the Erasmus Student Network, and in general a sort of high price on their activities

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries are mostly cheaper than in Denmark, especially fruit, greens and cheese
Coffee and alcohol is also cheaper
Rent is almost the same or even more expensive, which surprised me, but the monthly metro-card was really cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think both theatre and a sports day, but i didn't join

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I think there is a lot of beautiful cities around the Como, Maggiore and Garda lake, where you can easily take the train (use the trenitalia or Italo Treno app) - and the movie thatres are a lot cheaper than in Denmark

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In general very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I had two courses with the same master, so I saw them often which made it less anonymous, and easier to speak with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In the summertime, and a bit less later on, I think there was a lot of cat-calling on the streets, making it sometimes a bit uncomfortable to walk around.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The welcoming and relaxed spirit you meet at the coffee bars

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
That it's not a problem to take MA courses if you are a BA students, and likely the other students here will be more your own age 

It's a good idea to invest some time to get courses in order, but don't panic, they are helpful and you can change them if necessary

Look at what kind of exams the courses recquire if you are looking for a calmer december/january:)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to integrate in a different university and learning about topics that are not offered at home

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the way they do their exams are very different from what I am used to at pædagogik, so that was a bit challenging for me

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
